abstract: |
  Here we use the behavioural states estimated by the classification methods to identify where and when wedge-tailed eagles 'harvest' environmental energy by soaring. We select the fixes that most methods agree are soaring, split them into soaring bouts, and summarise the time spent soaring and the altitude gained through time and space. This creates the data that will be used to associate soaring with landscape features (such as elevation, topographic position and ridges) - the modelling and predictions are done in separate scripts.
---

# Load packages

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
packages <- c("leaflet", "terra", "tidyterra")
walk(packages, require, character.only = T)

```

# Import data from the model outputs

```{r}

kmeans_instantaneous <- read_csv("outputs/eagle_states_kmeans_instantaneous_Stella.csv")
kmeans_aggregated <- read_csv("outputs/eagle_states_kmeans_aggregated_Stella.csv")
kmeans_combined <- read_csv("outputs/eagle_states_kmeans_combined_Stella.csv")
hmm <- read_csv("outputs/eagle_states_hmm_Stella.csv")

```

## Join the dataframes

The dataframes have different numbers of rows, as some variables had NAs in some of the scripts but not others. We join them by the eagle's name and the start time of each step, and then only keep the fixes that were classified by all four methods.

We keep the location and flight variables from the k-means instantaneous data, and only the 3-state classifications from the others (plus the probability of the most likely state from the 3-state HMM).

```{r}

# number of rows in each dataframe
tibble(data = c("kmeans_instantaneous", "kmeans_aggregated", "kmeans_combined", "hmm"),
       rows = c(nrow(kmeans_instantaneous), nrow(kmeans_aggregated),
                nrow(kmeans_combined), nrow(hmm)))

eagle_states <- kmeans_combined %>%
  select(name, stepstart_dtime, stepend_dtime, 
         stepend_utme, stepend_utmn,
         flight_n, lat, lon,
         F_AOG, F_Sn, F_Vrate, F_radians, F_radians_abs, 
         F_turn_cum_window, F_speed_mean_window, F_Vrate_mean_window,
         kmeans_comb = k3) %>%
  full_join(kmeans_aggregated %>% select(name, stepstart_dtime, kmeans_agg = k3),
            by = c("name", "stepstart_dtime")) %>%
  full_join(kmeans_instantaneous %>% select(name, stepstart_dtime, kmeans_inst = k3),
            by = c("name", "stepstart_dtime")) %>%
  full_join(hmm %>% select(name, stepstart_dtime, hmm = hmm3, hmm3_prob),
            by = c("name", "stepstart_dtime"))

# number of rows after joining
nrow(eagle_states)

# drop rows that are missing a state from any of the methods
eagle_states <- eagle_states %>%
  drop_na(kmeans_inst, kmeans_agg, kmeans_comb, hmm)

# number of rows that were classified by all four methods
nrow(eagle_states)

```

## Label the states

The cluster (k-means) and state (HMM) numbers are arbitrary, so state 1 in one method isn't necessarily state 1 in another. Here we assign the same behaviour labels that were given to the 3-state models in each of the classification scripts.

Note that these need to match the labels in the classification scripts - if the models are re-run and the numbers change, update them here as well.

```{r}

# the names of the state columns, and labels to use in the plots
state_cols <- c("kmeans_inst", "kmeans_agg", "kmeans_comb", "hmm")

method_labels <- c(kmeans_inst = "K-means instantaneous",
                   kmeans_agg = "K-means aggregated",
                   kmeans_comb = "K-means combined",
                   hmm = "HMM instantaneous")

# colours that are used in all of the plots and the map
state_colours <- c(ascending = "#E69F00", flapping = "#56B4E9", gliding = "#009E73")

# the consensus state can also be 'no majority' (when fewer than 3 methods agree)
# consensus_colours <- c(state_colours, "no majority" = "#999999")
consensus_colours <- c(state_colours, "no majority" = "red")

agreement_colours <- c("all 4 agree" = "#0072B2",
                       "3 of 4 agree" = "#F0E442",
                       "no majority" = "#D55E00")

# the labels from each classification script
eagle_states <- eagle_states %>%
  mutate(
    
    kmeans_inst = case_when(kmeans_inst == 1 ~ "ascending",
                            kmeans_inst == 2 ~ "gliding",
                            kmeans_inst == 3 ~ "flapping"),
    
    kmeans_agg = case_when(kmeans_agg == 1 ~ "flapping",
                           kmeans_agg == 2 ~ "ascending",
                           kmeans_agg == 3 ~ "gliding"),
    
    kmeans_comb = case_when(kmeans_comb == 1 ~ "gliding",
                            kmeans_comb == 2 ~ "flapping",
                            kmeans_comb == 3 ~ "ascending"),
    
    hmm = case_when(hmm == 1 ~ "gliding",
                    hmm == 2 ~ "flapping",
                    hmm == 3 ~ "ascending")
    
    ) %>%
  # use the same factor levels for every method (so the colours are consistent)
  mutate(across(all_of(state_cols), \(x) factor(x, levels = names(state_colours))))

```

## Calculate the agreement between the methods

For each fix we count how many of the four methods classified it as each state. From this we get:

- `n_agree` - the number of methods that agree on the most common state (2, 3 or 4)
- `agreement` - whether all 4 methods agree, 3 of the 4 agree, or there is no majority (a 2-2 or 2-1-1 split)
- `consensus` - the state that at least 3 of the 4 methods agree on (otherwise 'no majority')
- `odd_one_out` - when 3 of the 4 methods agree, the method that disagrees

```{r}

eagle_states <- eagle_states %>%
  mutate(
    # the number of methods that classified each fix as each state
    n_ascending = rowSums(across(all_of(state_cols), \(x) x == "ascending")),
    n_flapping = rowSums(across(all_of(state_cols), \(x) x == "flapping")),
    n_gliding = rowSums(across(all_of(state_cols), \(x) x == "gliding")),

    # the number of methods that agree on the most common state
    n_agree = pmax(n_ascending, n_flapping, n_gliding),

    agreement = case_when(n_agree == 4 ~ "all 4 agree",
                          n_agree == 3 ~ "3 of 4 agree",
                          n_agree == 2 ~ "no majority"),

    # the state that at least 3 of the 4 methods agree on
    consensus = case_when(n_ascending >= 3 ~ "ascending",
                          n_flapping >= 3 ~ "flapping",
                          n_gliding >= 3 ~ "gliding",
                          TRUE ~ "no majority"),

    # when 3 of the 4 methods agree, which method disagrees?
    odd_one_out = case_when(n_agree != 3 ~ NA,
                            kmeans_inst != consensus ~ method_labels["kmeans_inst"],
                            kmeans_agg != consensus ~ method_labels["kmeans_agg"],
                            kmeans_comb != consensus ~ method_labels["kmeans_comb"],
                            hmm != consensus ~ method_labels["hmm"])
    ) %>%
  # set the order of the levels for plotting
  mutate(agreement = factor(agreement, levels = names(agreement_colours)),
         consensus = factor(consensus, levels = names(consensus_colours)),
         odd_one_out = factor(odd_one_out, levels = method_labels))

```

## Remove fixes below a minimum altitude

We want to exclude locations that are associated with taking off or landing.

```{r}

# to exclude fixes that are associated with taking off or landing
min_altitude <- 50 

eagle_states <- eagle_states %>% 
  filter(F_AOG >= min_altitude)

```

# Agreement through a flight segment

Choose a flight segment to explore, and look at the states from each method through time, along with the flight variables. The segment is chosen to be the one closest to *n* fixes, but you can change it to any other flight segment by changing `flight_n_explore` below.

```{r}

flight_length <- 1500 # in number of locations

# choose a flight segment - here the one closest to n locations
# (replace flight_n_explore with any other flight_n to explore a different flight)
flight_counts <- eagle_states %>% count(flight_n)
flight_n_explore <- flight_counts$flight_n[which.min(abs(flight_counts$n - flight_length))]

segment_explore <- eagle_states %>%
  filter(flight_n == flight_n_explore) %>%
  arrange(stepend_dtime) %>%
  # number the fixes in the segment
  mutate(fix = row_number())

```

The states from each method through a single flight segment, with the consensus state at the bottom. We use the same flight segment as in the classification scripts (the one closest to 1500 fixes), and the same segment is shown in the map below.

The whole segment is too dense to see clearly, so we only plot a window of 300 fixes (change `fix_window` to look at a different part of the segment).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

# the first and last fix to plot
fix_window <- c(1, 300)

segment_explore %>%
  filter(fix >= fix_window[1], fix <= fix_window[2]) %>%
  select(fix, all_of(state_cols), consensus) %>%
  # one row for each fix and method (as characters, as the factor levels differ)
  pivot_longer(-fix, names_to = "method", values_to = "state",
               values_transform = as.character) %>%
  mutate(method = factor(c(method_labels, consensus = "Consensus")[method],
                         levels = c(method_labels, "Consensus")),
         state = factor(state, levels = names(consensus_colours))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fix, y = method, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = consensus_colours) +
  # put the first method at the top
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Fix number in the flight segment", y = NULL, fill = "State") +
  theme_bw()

```

# Data explorer with states and agreement

The same data explorer as in the classification scripts, coloured by the agreement between methods, the consensus state, the states from each of the 3-state models, the probability of the most likely HMM state, and some of the flight variables. Use the 'Colour by' dropdown to switch between them, and hover over a fix to see all of the values.

```{r}

# the agreement and state variables, then the flight variables.
# The first variable is the one shown when the map loads
explore_vars <- c("agreement", "consensus", state_cols, "hmm3_prob",
                  "F_AOG", "F_Sn", "F_Vrate", "F_radians_abs")

# variables with negative and positive values get a diverging palette centred on 0
diverging_vars <- c("F_Vrate")

# colours for the categorical variables (the same as in the plots above)
map_colours <- list(agreement = agreement_colours,
                    consensus = consensus_colours,
                    kmeans_inst = state_colours,
                    kmeans_agg = state_colours,
                    kmeans_comb = state_colours,
                    hmm = state_colours)

# the same function as in the classification scripts, with one addition - the
# 'colours' argument, which sets the colours of categorical variables
flight_explorer <- function(segment, vars, diverging = character(0), colours = list(), height = 650) {

  segment <- segment %>% arrange(stepend_dtime)
  n_fix <- nrow(segment)

  # hover labels - timestamp and the (unclipped) value of every variable
  label_rows <- map(vars, \(v) {
    val <- segment[[v]]
    val <- if (is.numeric(val)) as.character(round(val, 3)) else as.character(val)
    paste0("<tr><td>", v, "</td>",
           "<td style='text-align:right; padding-left:10px;'><b>", val, "</b></td></tr>")
  })
  labels <- paste0("<b>", format(segment$stepend_dtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "</b>",
                   " (fix ", seq_len(n_fix), " of ", n_fix, ")",
                   "<table>", reduce(label_rows, paste0), "</table>") %>%
    map(htmltools::HTML)

  # colour palette for each variable
  make_palette <- function(x, v) {
    if (!is.numeric(x)) {
      okabe_ito <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
                     "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#999999")
      # keep the levels of factors (so states missing from this segment don't shift the colours)
      if (!is.factor(x)) x <- factor(x)
      # use the colours given for this variable, otherwise the Okabe-Ito palette
      cols <- if (v %in% names(colours)) colours[[v]][levels(x)] else okabe_ito[seq_along(levels(x))]
      pal <- colorFactor(cols, domain = NULL, levels = levels(x))
      return(list(pal = pal, x = x))
    }
    lims <- quantile(x, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
    if (v %in% diverging) {
      lims <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(lims))
      pal <- colorNumeric("RdBu", domain = lims, reverse = TRUE)
    } else {
      pal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = lims)
    }
    list(pal = pal, x = pmin(pmax(x, lims[1]), lims[2])) # clip to the colour range
  }

  palettes <- map(set_names(vars), \(v) make_palette(segment[[v]], v))
  # the point colours for each variable (switched in the browser by the dropdown)
  point_colours <- map(palettes, \(p) p$pal(p$x))

  # a single layer of points (so the hover labels aren't duplicated for every variable)
  m <- leaflet(segment, height = height, width = "100%",
               options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
    addPolylines(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, color = "white", weight = 1,
                 opacity = 0.6, group = "Flight path") %>%
    addCircleMarkers(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, radius = 4, stroke = FALSE,
                     fillColor = point_colours[[1]], fillOpacity = 0.9,
                     layerId = paste0("fix", seq_len(n_fix)), label = labels,
                     labelOptions = labelOptions(textsize = "12px", direction = "auto"))

  # one legend per variable - only the selected one is shown
  for (v in vars) {
    m <- m %>%
      addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = palettes[[v]]$pal, values = palettes[[v]]$x,
                title = v, opacity = 1, className = paste0("info legend legend-var legend-", v))
  }

  m %>%
    addLayersControl(overlayGroups = "Flight path",
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) %>%
    addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft") %>%
    # add a 'Colour by' dropdown that recolours the points and switches the legend
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el, x, data) {
        var map = this;
        function colourBy(v) {
          var cols = data.cols[v];
          for (var i = 1; i <= data.n; i++) {
            var m = map.layerManager.getLayer('marker', 'fix' + i);
            if (m) m.setStyle({fillColor: cols[i - 1]});
          }
          el.querySelectorAll('.legend-var').forEach(function(l) {
            l.style.display = l.classList.contains('legend-' + v) ? '' : 'none';
          });
        }
        // leaflet only draws the layers once the map is visible (e.g. inside
        // a tab), so wait until the points exist before adding the dropdown
        function setup() {
          if (!map.layerManager || !map.layerManager.getLayer('marker', 'fix1')) {
            setTimeout(setup, 200);
            return;
          }
          addDropdown();
        }
        setup();
        function addDropdown() {
          var ctrl = L.control({position: 'topright'});
          ctrl.onAdd = function() {
            var div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'info legend');
            div.innerHTML = '<b>Colour by</b><br><select style=\"margin-top:4px;\">' +
              data.vars.map(function(v) {
                return '<option value=\"' + v + '\">' + v + '</option>';
              }).join('') + '</select>';
            div.querySelector('select').addEventListener('change', function() {
              colourBy(this.value);
            });
            L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div);
            L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(div);
            return div;
          };
          ctrl.addTo(map);
          colourBy(data.vars[0]);
        }
      }", data = list(vars = vars, cols = point_colours, n = n_fix))
}

flight_explorer(segment_explore, explore_vars, diverging = diverging_vars, colours = map_colours)

```

# Quantifying energy harvesting

## Pull out just the ascending state (soaring)

We keep only the fixes that at least 3 of the 4 methods classified as ascending, and then split them into separate soaring bouts.

For each soaring fix we calculate the gap between the end of the previous soaring step and the start of this one, which is the time that the eagle spent doing something else (gliding, flapping, or a fix with no majority). Consecutive soaring steps have a gap of 0 seconds. A new bout starts when:

- the gap is longer than `max_gap_s` (60 seconds), or
- (optional, currently commented out) the soaring fix is in a different flight segment to the previous one. Flight segments are separated by gaps in the data of at least ~30 seconds (where the eagle may have landed), so this stops a bout continuing across them even when the gap is less than 60 seconds. Uncomment the `flight_n != lag(flight_n)` line to add this condition.

Short interruptions (e.g. a few fixes of gliding between thermals, or a misclassified fix) therefore stay within the same bout.

Bouts that are shorter than `min_bout_s` are removed in the next section, as these are often only a few fixes (sometimes just one) and are more likely to be brief climbs or misclassifications than thermal or slope soaring.

```{r}

# the longest gap (in seconds) between soaring fixes within the same bout
max_gap_s <- 60

# the shortest bout (in seconds) to keep - shorter bouts are removed below
min_bout_s <- 30

# split soaring into bouts if there are gaps more than max_gap_s seconds
eagle_states <- eagle_states %>%
  # put the fixes in time order for each eagle
  arrange(name, stepstart_dtime) %>%
  group_by(name, consensus) %>%
  mutate(
    # time (s) between the end of the previous soaring step and the start of this one
    gap_s = as.numeric(difftime(stepstart_dtime, lag(stepend_dtime), units = "secs")),
    # TRUE when this fix starts a new bout - the first soaring fix of each eagle
    # (where gap_s is NA), after a long gap, or in a new flight segment
    new_bout = is.na(gap_s) |
      gap_s > max_gap_s, # |
      # flight_n != lag(flight_n),
    # number the bouts for each eagle (cumsum counts up by 1 at every new bout)
    bout_n = cumsum(new_bout)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # a unique id for each bout (in case there are multiple eagles)
  mutate(bout_id = paste(name, consensus, bout_n, sep = "_"))

```

## Split into the different states

```{r}

soaring_locations <- eagle_states %>% filter(consensus == "ascending")
# number of soaring fixes and soaring bouts
paste0("Number of soaring locations = ", nrow(soaring_locations))
paste0("Number of soaring bouts = ", n_distinct(soaring_locations$bout_id))

flapping_locations <- eagle_states %>% filter(consensus == "flapping")
# number of flapping fixes and flapping bouts
paste0("Number of flapping locations = ", nrow(flapping_locations))
paste0("Number of flapping bouts = ", n_distinct(flapping_locations$bout_id))

```

## Summarise each soaring bout

For each bout we calculate:

- `duration_s` - the time from the start of the first soaring step to the end of the last soaring step (including any short gaps)
- `soaring_s` - the time spent soaring (the sum of the soaring step durations, so excluding the gaps)
- `alt_gain_m` - the altitude gained while soaring (vertical rate × step duration, summed over the soaring steps)
- `mean_Vrate` - the mean vertical rate (m/s) of the soaring fixes

We then remove the bouts with a `duration_s` shorter than `min_bout_s`, and the soaring fixes from those bouts, so that everything below only uses the bouts that are at least 60 seconds long.

```{r}

soaring_bouts <- soaring_locations %>%
  # duration of each step (s)
  mutate(step_s = as.numeric(difftime(stepend_dtime, stepstart_dtime, units = "secs"))) %>%
  # (bout_n before bout_id, so the bouts stay in time order)
  group_by(name, bout_n, bout_id) %>%
  summarise(
    flight_n = first(flight_n),
    start = min(stepstart_dtime),
    end = max(stepend_dtime),
    n_fixes = n(),
    duration_s = as.numeric(difftime(end, start, units = "secs")),
    soaring_s = sum(step_s),
    alt_gain_m = sum(F_Vrate * step_s),
    mean_Vrate = mean(F_Vrate),
    # the start of the bout (in UTM for ggplot and lat/lon for leaflet)
    utme = first(stepend_utme, order_by = stepstart_dtime),
    utmn = first(stepend_utmn, order_by = stepstart_dtime),
    lat  = first(lat,          order_by = stepstart_dtime),
    lon  = first(lon,          order_by = stepstart_dtime),
    # the centre of the bout (in UTM for ggplot and lat/lon for leaflet)
    utme_mean = mean(stepend_utme),
    utmn_mean = mean(stepend_utmn),
    lat_mean = mean(lat),
    lon_mean = mean(lon),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# number of bouts before removing the short ones
nrow(soaring_bouts)

# remove the bouts that are shorter than min_bout_s
soaring_bouts <- soaring_bouts %>% filter(duration_s >= min_bout_s)

# and remove the soaring fixes that were in those short bouts
soaring_locations <- soaring_locations %>% filter(bout_id %in% soaring_bouts$bout_id)

# number of bouts and soaring fixes that are left
nrow(soaring_bouts)
nrow(soaring_locations)

soaring_bouts

```

## Summarise the flapping bouts

We do the same as above but for the flapping bouts.

```{r}

flapping_bouts <- flapping_locations %>%
  # duration of each step (s)
  mutate(step_s = as.numeric(difftime(stepend_dtime, stepstart_dtime, units = "secs"))) %>%
  # (bout_n before bout_id, so the bouts stay in time order)
  group_by(name, bout_n, bout_id) %>%
  summarise(
    flight_n = first(flight_n),
    start = min(stepstart_dtime),
    end = max(stepend_dtime),
    n_fixes = n(),
    duration_s = as.numeric(difftime(end, start, units = "secs")),
    flapping_s = sum(step_s),
    alt_gain_m = sum(F_Vrate * step_s),
    mean_Vrate = mean(F_Vrate),
    # the start of the bout (in UTM for ggplot and lat/lon for leaflet)
    utme = first(stepend_utme, order_by = stepstart_dtime),
    utmn = first(stepend_utmn, order_by = stepstart_dtime),
    lat  = first(lat,          order_by = stepstart_dtime),
    lon  = first(lon,          order_by = stepstart_dtime),
    # the centre of the bout (in UTM for ggplot and lat/lon for leaflet)
    utme_mean = mean(stepend_utme),
    utmn_mean = mean(stepend_utmn),
    lat_mean = mean(lat),
    lon_mean = mean(lon),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# number of bouts before removing the short ones
nrow(flapping_bouts)

# remove the bouts that are shorter than min_bout_s
flapping_bouts <- flapping_bouts %>% filter(duration_s >= min_bout_s)

# and remove the flapping fixes that were in those short bouts
flapping_locations <- flapping_locations %>% filter(bout_id %in% flapping_bouts$bout_id)

# number of bouts and flapping fixes that are left
nrow(flapping_bouts)
nrow(flapping_locations)

flapping_bouts

```

## Time spent soaring

The total time spent soaring (in bouts of at least `min_bout_s`), compared to the total flight time (the sum of the step durations of all of the fixes that were classified by all four methods).

```{r}

# total flight time and soaring time (hours) for each eagle
eagle_states %>%
  mutate(step_s = as.numeric(difftime(stepend_dtime, stepstart_dtime, units = "secs"))) %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  summarise(flight_h = sum(step_s) / 3600) %>%
  left_join(soaring_bouts %>%
              group_by(name) %>%
              summarise(n_bouts = n(),
                        soaring_h = sum(soaring_s) / 3600),
            by = "name") %>%
  mutate(prop_soaring = soaring_h / flight_h)

```

# Behaviours through time

The timestamps are in UTC, so we convert them to local Tasmanian time (which accounts for daylight saving) before getting the date and hour of the day.

For each fix we also calculate the altitude gained or lost during that step (`step_alt_gain_m`), so that the altitude gained in each hour or day comes from the fixes in that hour or day (a bout that runs from 11:55 to 12:10 is split between the 11:00 and 12:00 hours). The number of bouts is counted by the time that each bout started.

As well as the number of bouts and the altitude gained, we calculate the proportion of the flight time in that behaviour. This accounts for there being more soaring bouts at times when the eagle is flying more (and when there is more tracking data).

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Soaring locations

```{r}

# local time zone (Tasmania)
local_tz <- "Australia/Hobart"

# add the step duration, local time, date and hour to the flight data
eagle_states <- eagle_states %>%
  mutate(step_s = as.numeric(difftime(stepend_dtime, stepstart_dtime, units = "secs")),
         local_time = with_tz(stepstart_dtime, local_tz),
         date = as_date(local_time),
         hour = hour(local_time))

# and to the soaring fixes, with the altitude gained during each step
soaring_locations <- soaring_locations %>%
  mutate(step_s = as.numeric(difftime(stepend_dtime, stepstart_dtime, units = "secs")),
         step_alt_gain_m = F_Vrate * step_s,
         local_time = with_tz(stepstart_dtime, local_tz),
         date = as_date(local_time),
         hour = hour(local_time))

# and the start of each soaring bout
soaring_bouts <- soaring_bouts %>%
  mutate(start_local = with_tz(start, local_tz),
         date = as_date(start_local),
         hour = hour(start_local))

# labels for the panels in the plots below
time_labels <- c(n_bouts = "Number of soaring bouts",
                 alt_gain_m = "Altitude gained while soaring (m)",
                 prop_soaring = "Proportion of flight time spent soaring")

```

### Hour of the day

The totals for each hour of the day, across all of the days (and eagles).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7

# flight time in each hour
soaring_hourly <- eagle_states %>%
  group_by(hour) %>%
  summarise(flight_h = sum(step_s) / 3600) %>%
  # number of bouts that started in each hour
  left_join(soaring_bouts %>% count(hour, name = "n_bouts"),
            by = "hour") %>%
  # altitude gained and time spent soaring in each hour
  left_join(soaring_locations %>%
              group_by(hour) %>%
              summarise(alt_gain_m = sum(step_alt_gain_m),
                        soaring_h = sum(step_s) / 3600),
            by = "hour") %>%
  # hours with flight but no soaring have 0 bouts and 0 altitude gained
  mutate(across(c(n_bouts, alt_gain_m, soaring_h), \(x) replace_na(x, 0)),
         prop_soaring = soaring_h / flight_h)

soaring_hourly

soaring_hourly %>%
  pivot_longer(c(n_bouts, alt_gain_m, prop_soaring), names_to = "variable") %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(time_labels[variable], levels = time_labels)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_col(aes(x = hour, y = value), fill = state_colours["ascending"]) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Hour of the day (local time)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

```

The daily totals through the tracking period. Days where the eagle didn't fly (or had no data) are left blank.

```{r}
            by = "date") %>%
  # altitude gained and time spent soaring on each day
  left_join(soaring_locations %>%
```

# Where do the eagles show different behaviours?

## Spatial layers

We read in the spatial layers and crop them to the area around all of the flight locations (plus a buffer), so they are quick to plot. We use all of the flight locations rather than only the soaring locations so that the grid used to calculate the proportion of time soaring (below) covers the areas where the eagles flew but didn't soar. Add any other rasters to `raster_files` to include them in the leaflet map below - the names are used as the layer names in the map.

The rasters are at 30 m resolution. If the soaring locations cover a large area (e.g. when using all eagles), uncomment the `aggregate()` line to use a coarser resolution, otherwise the maps will be slow and the leaflet map may hit its size limit.

```{r}

# the spatial layers to crop (and add to the leaflet map)
raster_files <- c(elevation = "mapping/HS_DEM.tif",
                  tpi_300m = "mapping/TPI_300m.tif",
                  slope = "mapping/HS_Slope.tif",
                  ruggedness = "mapping/HS_Ruggedness.tif",
                  aspect = "mapping/Aspect_degrees.tif")

# the area to crop to - the extent of all of the flight locations plus a buffer (m)
buffer_m <- 2000

crop_area <- ext(min(eagle_states$stepend_utme) - buffer_m,
                 max(eagle_states$stepend_utme) + buffer_m,
                 min(eagle_states$stepend_utmn) - buffer_m,
                 max(eagle_states$stepend_utmn) + buffer_m) %>%
  # the eagle locations are in GDA94 / MGA zone 55
  vect(crs = "EPSG:28355")

# read in and crop each raster (the crop area is projected to the crs of each
# raster, in case some are in a different crs)
spatial_layers <- map(raster_files, \(f) {
  r <- rast(f)
  r <- crop(r, project(crop_area, crs(r)))
  # r <- aggregate(r, fact = 5) # 5 x 5 cells, i.e. 150 m resolution
  r
})

spatial_layers

```

## Interactive map

The centre of each soaring bout over a satellite (or topographic) basemap, coloured by the altitude gained in that bout. Hover over a bout to see its details. The spatial layers are added as overlays that can be switched on in the layer control (top right) - they are hidden when the map loads.

```{r}

# colour palette for the altitude gained in each bout
bout_palette <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = soaring_bouts$alt_gain_m)

# hover labels for each bout
bout_labels <- paste0("<b>", soaring_bouts$bout_id, "</b><br>",
                      format(soaring_bouts$start_local, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), "<br>",
                      "Duration: ", round(soaring_bouts$duration_s / 60, 1), " min<br>",
                      "Altitude gained: ", round(soaring_bouts$alt_gain_m), " m<br>",
                      "Mean vertical rate: ", round(soaring_bouts$mean_Vrate, 2), " m/s") %>%
  map(htmltools::HTML)

# basemaps
soaring_map <- leaflet(soaring_bouts, height = 650, width = "100%",
                       options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "Satellite") %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$OpenTopoMap, group = "Topographic")

# add each spatial layer (in greyscale, so the bouts stand out), with its own legend
for (layer in names(spatial_layers)) {

  r <- spatial_layers[[layer]]
  layer_palette <- colorNumeric("Greys", domain = range(values(r), na.rm = TRUE),
                                na.color = "transparent", reverse = TRUE)

  soaring_map <- soaring_map %>%
    addRasterImage(r, colors = layer_palette, opacity = 0.8, group = layer) %>%
    addLegend(position = "bottomleft", pal = layer_palette,
              values = range(values(r), na.rm = TRUE), title = layer, group = layer)
}

soaring_map %>%
  addCircleMarkers(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, radius = 4, stroke = FALSE,
                   fillColor = ~bout_palette(alt_gain_m), fillOpacity = 0.9,
                   label = bout_labels, group = "Soaring bouts") %>%
  addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = bout_palette, values = ~alt_gain_m,
            title = "Altitude gained (m)", group = "Soaring bouts") %>%
  addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satellite", "Topographic"),
                   overlayGroups = c(names(spatial_layers), "Soaring bouts"),
                   options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) %>%
  # hide the spatial layers when the map loads
  hideGroup(names(spatial_layers)) %>%
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft")

```

# Calculate the proportion of time soaring

For every cell, we calculate the total time spent soaring (the sum of the step durations of the soaring fixes in that cell) and the total flight time (the sum of the step durations of all fixes in that cell). The proportion of time spent soaring is then the soaring time divided by the flight time.

The grid is made by aggregating the 30 m elevation raster into larger cells (`cell_size_m`), so that the cells line up with the spatial layers, and the landscape variables can be aggregated to exactly the same cells for the modelling. Smaller cells match the landscape features more closely, but have fewer fixes in each, so the proportions are noisier (for Stella, the median number of fixes in a cell is 9 at 30 m, compared to 65 at 150 m). `cell_size_m` needs to be a multiple of 30 m.

Each fix is assigned to a cell by the location at the end of its step (the same location used in the maps above).

- The flight time includes every fix that was classified by all four methods (including fixes with no majority), as in the 'Time spent soaring' section above.
- The soaring time only includes the soaring fixes in bouts of at least `min_bout_s`, so the soaring fixes in shorter bouts count towards the flight time but not the soaring time.
- The cells are combined across eagles. To calculate them separately for each eagle, add `name` to both `group_by()` calls (the maps would then need to be filtered to one eagle).

## Behvaioural time in each cell

```{r}

# size of the grid cells (m) - a multiple of the 30 m resolution of the spatial layers
cell_size_m <- 150

# make the grid by combining the 30 m elevation cells into larger cells
# (fact is the number of 30 m cells along each side of a larger cell)
behaviour_grid <- aggregate(spatial_layers$elevation,
                          fact = cell_size_m / res(spatial_layers$elevation)[1])

behaviour_grid

# the grid cell that each fix is in (from the end location of each step)
eagle_states <- eagle_states %>%
  mutate(cell = cellFromXY(behaviour_grid, cbind(stepend_utme, stepend_utmn)))

soaring_locations <- soaring_locations %>%
  mutate(cell = cellFromXY(behaviour_grid, cbind(stepend_utme, stepend_utmn)))

flapping_locations <- flapping_locations %>%
  mutate(cell = cellFromXY(behaviour_grid, cbind(stepend_utme, stepend_utmn)))

# check that all of the fixes are inside the grid (this should be 0)
sum(is.na(eagle_states$cell))

# flight time in each cell
behaviour_cells <- eagle_states %>%
  group_by(cell) %>%
  summarise(n_fixes = n(),
            flight_s = sum(step_s)) %>%
  # soaring time in each cell
  left_join(soaring_locations %>%
              group_by(cell) %>%
              summarise(n_soaring_fixes = n(),
                        soaring_s = sum(step_s)),
            by = "cell") %>%
  # flapping time in each cell
  left_join(flapping_locations %>%
              group_by(cell) %>%
              summarise(n_flapping_fixes = n(),
                        flapping_s = sum(step_s)),
            by = "cell") %>%
  mutate(
    # cells with flight but no soaring have 0 soaring time
    across(c(n_soaring_fixes, soaring_s), \(x) replace_na(x, 0)),
    across(c(n_flapping_fixes, flapping_s), \(x) replace_na(x, 0)),
    prop_soaring = soaring_s / flight_s,
    prop_flapping = flapping_s / flight_s,
    # the coordinates of the centre of each cell
    x = xFromCell(behaviour_grid, cell),
    y = yFromCell(behaviour_grid, cell)
  )

behaviour_cells

# number of cells with flight, and the number of those with some soaring
nrow(behaviour_cells)
sum(behaviour_cells$soaring_s > 0)
sum(behaviour_cells$flapping_s > 0)

```

```{r}
            aes(x = x, y = y, fill = flight_s / 60),
            width = cell_size_m, height = cell_size_m) +

                          breaks = seq(0, 2000, by = contour_m),
                          colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
```

```{r}
            width = cell_size_m, height = cell_size_m) +
  geom_spatraster_contour(data = spatial_layers$elevation,
                          breaks = seq(0, 2000, by = contour_m),
                          colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Soaring time\n(minutes)") +
  theme_bw()

```

## Flapping time

The flapping time in each cell (on a log scale).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = behaviour_cells,
            aes(x = x, y = y, fill = flapping_s / 60),
            width = cell_size_m, height = cell_size_m) +
  geom_spatraster_contour(data = spatial_layers$elevation,
                          breaks = seq(0, 2000, by = contour_m),
                          colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Flapping time\n(minutes)") +
  theme_bw()

```

## Proprtion soaring

The proportion of the flight time spent soaring in each cell. Cells with only a few fixes can only have a few values (e.g. a cell with 1 fix is either 0 or 1), so we only show the cells with at least `min_cell_fixes` fixes (the other cells are still in `soaring_cells`).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

# the minimum number of fixes in a cell to show it in the map
min_cell_fixes <- 10

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = behaviour_cells %>% filter(n_fixes >= min_cell_fixes),
            aes(x = x, y = y, fill = prop_soaring),
            width = cell_size_m, height = cell_size_m) +
  geom_spatraster_contour(data = spatial_layers$elevation,
                          breaks = seq(0, 2000, by = contour_m),
                          colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Proportion\nof time\nsoaring") +
  theme_bw()

# distribution of the proportion of time soaring across the cells
behaviour_cells %>%
  filter(n_fixes >= min_cell_fixes) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = prop_soaring), bins = 50) +
  labs(x = "Proportion of time soaring in the cell", y = "Number of cells") +
  theme_bw()

```

The proportion of the flight time spent flapping in each cell. Cells with only a few fixes can only have a few values (e.g. a cell with 1 fix is either 0 or 1), so we only show the cells with at least `min_cell_fixes` fixes (the other cells are still in `flapping_cells`).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

# the minimum number of fixes in a cell to show it in the map
min_cell_fixes <- 10

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = behaviour_cells %>% filter(n_fixes >= min_cell_fixes),
            aes(x = x, y = y, fill = prop_flapping),
            width = cell_size_m, height = cell_size_m) +
  geom_spatraster_contour(data = spatial_layers$elevation,
                          breaks = seq(0, 2000, by = contour_m),
                          colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Proportion\nof time\nflapping") +
  theme_bw()

# distribution of the proportion of time flapping across the cells
behaviour_cells %>%
  filter(n_fixes >= min_cell_fixes) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = prop_flapping), bins = 50) +
  labs(x = "Proportion of time flapping in the cell", y = "Number of cells") +
  theme_bw()

```

:::

## Prevalence of soaring

There are multiple different ways that we could associate climbing behaviour with landscape variables to predict where wedge-tailed eagles are harvesting environmental energy.

- Presence of soaring (positive vertical rate) in that cell
- Occurrence of soaring (presence of uplifts) and flapping flight (absence of uplifts) (as per @Scacco2019-si)
- Proportion of time spent soaring in that cell, compared to the total proportion of time spent in that cell
- Average positive vertical rate (of the soaring behaviour only)
- Maximum positive vertical rate (of the soaring behaviour only)

For now, we'll take the soaring bouts, with individual soaring bouts = 1, and non-soaring bouts = 0, and model the probability of soaring in a cell as a function of the landscape variables. This is similar to @Scacco2019-si, but we are using the bouts rather than 15-second groups of fixes.
